record.paper_title: Physical Layer Security in Satellite Communication: State-of-the-art and Open Problems
record.original_question: How can physical-layer security authentication and anti-spoofing strategies be designed for satellite services beyond global navigation satellite systems, including broadband and satellite-IoT services, so that unauthorized devices cannot impersonate legitimate users or inject high-power spoofed signals and unauthenticated messages that grant illicit service access or leak information intended for legitimate users?

evidence.quote: However, other types of satellites used in other services, such as broadband and IoT connection, are vulnerable to spoofing or impersonation attacks that affect their service and give access to unauthorized devices.

In wireless systems such as satellites, the adversary sends signals with higher power than the legitimate user to deceive the receiver into considering his spoofed message as the legitimate one[83]. Hence, the adversary will get access to the service and information intended for the legitimate user. As a result, anti-spoofing PLS strategies need investigation in satellite scenarios with different services to prevent unauthenticated access or information leakage.

artifact.status_search_result: Physical-layer authentication and anti-spoofing for non-GNSS satellite services (broadband, satellite-IoT) remains an actively researched open area. Recent surveys and papers (2023–2025) on LEO/6G non-terrestrial network security continue to list satellite PLS authentication against impersonation and overshadowing as unresolved, with proposed schemes (RF fingerprinting, CSI-based authentication, Doppler-based methods) offering partial solutions without comprehensive formal guarantees under high-power spoofing.

status_evidence.title: Physical Layer Security in Satellite Communication: State-of-the-art and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Anti-spoofing PLS strategies need investigation in satellite scenarios with different services to prevent unauthenticated access or information leakage.
status_evidence.claim: The problem of PLS-based anti-spoofing and authentication for non-GNSS satellite services is explicitly listed as an open research direction.

status_evidence.title: Security in Non-Terrestrial Networks: Challenges and Open Issues (survey, 2024)
status_evidence.snippet: Authentication and spoofing detection in LEO satellite broadband and IoT links remain open, with current PLS proposals lacking unified guarantees against high-power adversaries.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent surveys continue to mark satellite PLS authentication beyond GNSS as open.
